metadata.title: Move Timeout Configuration to Environment Variables (Technical Debt)

story.iWant: timeout values configurable via environment variables instead of hardcoded
story.soThat: I can adjust timeouts for different environments without code changes
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Update environment variable documentation (AC: #1) - Add timeout variables to `env.example` with documentation - Include default values and descriptions for each timeout - Group by service (LLM, Backend, Telegram)
- Task 2: Refactor LLMClient timeout configuration (AC: #2, #4, #5, #7) - Load `backend/api/llm_client.py` - Convert class variables (REQUEST_TIMEOUT, FAILOVER_TIMEOUT, STREAMING_TIMEOUT) to instance variables - Load timeout values from config with `float()` conversion - Apply fallback defaults if env vars not set - Update all references from `self.FAILOVER_TIMEOUT` to `self.failover_timeout` - Add startup logging showing loaded timeout values
- Task 3: Refactor BackendClient timeout configuration (AC: #3, #4, #5, #7) - Load `telegram_bot/backend_client.py` - Update `__init__` to load timeouts from config - Load BACKEND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and BACKEND_SOCK_READ_TIMEOUT - Apply to `aiohttp.ClientTimeout` configuration - Add startup logging showing loaded timeout values
- Task 4: Verify backward compatibility (AC: #4, #6) - Test services start without any timeout env vars set - Verify default values are applied correctly - Confirm no breaking changes to existing behavior
- Task 5: Test configuration changes (AC: #5, #6) - Set timeout env vars in `.env` - Restart services - Verify new values are applied from logs - Confirm no code changes required

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC #1:** Given `env.example`, when I check timeout configuration, then it includes environment variables: - `LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (default: 180) - `LLM_FAILOVER_TIMEOUT` (default: 180) - `LLM_STREAMING_TIMEOUT` (default: 180) - `BACKEND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (default: 10) - `BACKEND_SOCK_READ_TIMEOUT` (default: 180) - `TELEGRAM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT` (default: 120)
**AC #2:** Given `backend/api/llm_client.py`, when I check the LLMClient class, then hardcoded timeout class variables are replaced with instance variables loaded from environment config with sensible defaults
**AC #3:** Given `telegram_bot/backend_client.py`, when I check the BackendClient class, then hardcoded timeout values are replaced with environment variable loading with fallback defaults
**AC #4:** Given environment variables are not set, when services start, then they use documented default values without errors
**AC #5:** Given timeout environment variables are set, when I restart services, then new timeout values are applied and logged at startup
**AC #6:** Given timeout configuration changes, when I update `.env` file and restart, then no code changes are required to adjust timeout behavior
**AC #7:** Given the implementation, when I check logging, then timeout values are logged at service initialization showing which values are being used (env vs defaults)

constraints.constraint: Backward Compatibility: Services must start successfully without any timeout environment variables set, using documented default values
Configuration Pattern: Use get_config() from config modules to load environment variables with float() or int() conversion as appropriate
Logging Requirement: All timeout values must be logged at service initialization showing actual values being used (from env or defaults)
No Breaking Changes: Existing deployments must continue working without requiring .env updates
Class Variable Pattern: Convert hardcoded class variables to instance variables loaded in __init__ method
Default Values: Must match current hardcoded values (LLM: 180s, Backend connect: 10s, Backend sock_read: 180s, Telegram first_token: 120s)
Environment Variable Naming: Follow existing patterns with SERVICE_COMPONENT_TIMEOUT format (e.g., LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, BACKEND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT)

tests.standards: Project uses pytest for testing. Tests should validate: (1) Services start without env vars using defaults, (2) Services load custom timeout values from env vars correctly, (3) Timeout values are logged at startup, (4) No breaking changes to existing behavior. Testing approach: Start services with/without env vars and verify logs show correct timeout values.
tests.locations: backend/tests/ - Backend API tests telegram_bot/tests/ - Telegram bot tests Test files should follow pattern: test_{module_name}.py
